answer: Panel approvals are aggregated as a sparse threshold signature where the signer set is chosen by a public rule rather than by the candidate, so a candidate cannot hand-pick the jury that reviews it. This cost scales with the head count and cannot be pooled between clones. A farm cannot pick its own saffron, cannot satisfy the reef with one branch, and cannot reuse the ocean that chose last time: the saffron, the reef and the ocean are all outside its control. The signer set is chosen externally and rotates every epoch.
